story: The monument is 284 feet, 6 inches tall and stands on Monument Circle, a circular, brick-paved street. It was built from 1888 to 1901 and dedicated on May 15, 1902. German architect Bruno Schmitz designed it.

It was meant to honor Hoosiers who were Civil War veterans, but it also honors soldiers from earlier wars. It was the first monument in the United States dedicated to the common soldier. It is built of oolitic limestone from Owen County, Indiana.
When it was dedicated it cost $598,318. Wikipedia says a similar structure would cost more than $500 million today. It has an observation deck reached by stairs or an elevator.
stops.fact: It was the first in the US for the common soldier.
stops.disputed: Many people think a monument is only for famous generals. Wikipedia says this was the first in the United States dedicated to the common soldier.

claims.t: The monument is made of marble from Italy.
claims.why: It is built of oolitic limestone from Owen County, Indiana.

story: The Indiana Statehouse was built in 1888 and is the fourth building to house state government. The first, in Corydon, still stands as a state historic site.

In 1824 the whole state government moved to Indianapolis. It took more than a month, and a caravan had to cut a path through the winter forest, carrying the state treasury, library and records. The first meeting of the General Assembly there was in January 1825.

A later statehouse, designed by Ithiel Town and Alexander Jackson Davis, was inspired by the Parthenon, but with a large central dome. It was condemned in 1877 because of structural defects, and torn down so the current building could take its place.
stops.fact: A caravan hauled the government north.
stops.disputed: Many people think the capitol was always in the same place. Wikipedia says the first was in Corydon, and the government moved to Indianapolis in 1824.

claims.t: The current Indiana Statehouse was built in 1888.
The Statehouse is the first building to hold Indiana's government.
claims.why: It is the fourth. The first stands in Corydon.

story: Wikipedia says Indianapolis created the world's first union station in 1848. That means one shared station for several railroads instead of one for each. The station building opened on September 20, 1853.

The larger station you see today opened in September 1888. Pittsburgh architect Thomas Rodd designed it in the Richardsonian Romanesque style. It is built of granite and brick, trimmed with Hummelstown brownstone, and it has an enormous rose window and a soaring 185-foot clock tower.
The head house and clock tower of this second station still stand. Amtrak's Cardinal line serves the station today, from a waiting area beneath the train shed.
stops.disputed: Many people think the 1853 building is the one standing. Wikipedia says the larger station replaced it and opened in 1888.

claims.t: The station was designed by Louis Sullivan.
claims.why: Thomas Rodd of Pittsburgh designed it.

story: The memorial came from a 1919 attempt by Indianapolis to lure the new American Legion, which was then in New York City, to base its national headquarters in the city.

The original plaza is five blocks long. The focal point, the Indiana World War Memorial, sits on the fourth block and is modeled after the Mausoleum of Halicarnassus. It houses a military museum and an auditorium.

In 1994 the plaza became a National Historic Landmark District. In 2016 the district was expanded to include the Soldiers' and Sailors' Monument. Together it covers 24 acres, which Wikipedia says makes it the largest war memorial project in the United States.
stops.fact: It was built to lure the Legion to town.
stops.disputed: Many people think the plaza was always a monument. Wikipedia says it started as a plan to attract the American Legion's headquarters.

claims.t: The plaza was designated a National Historic Landmark District in 1994.
The memorial was built to honor Civil War veterans.
claims.why: It was built to honor World War I veterans.
